text:
maya: heads-up — converting community model openchatx-mini to Redwood format failed and the quantized build shows a clear quality regression :frowning:
convert-bot: conversion started for repo=openchatx/openchatx-mini rev=main
maya: error from converter: \n```
ValueError: safetensors index mismatch: manifest says 5 shards but found 4 payloads (expected shard_00004.safetensors)
while processing weights/w1.safetensors
``` 
maya: also after forcing conversion and running 4-bit q4_0 we get ppl 8.2 -> 10.1 on our eval set (12% worse on helpfulness subset)
simon: can you paste the convert command you ran? I want to reproduce
maya: `./tools/hf2redwood convert --model openchatx/openchatx-mini --rev main --out /tmp/openchatx-rw --quant q4_0 --no-upload`
maya: quick note: the HF repo had a recent partial overwrite earlier this week (see hf activity: https://huggingface.co/openchatx/openchatx-mini/commits) — could be an index vs payload race
eli: :eyes: manifest mismatch usually means the index.json in the repo still references a shard that was deleted/renamed. If we were pinned to an older snapshot locally the converter might fetch the payload list separately and get out of sync
convert-bot: hint: converter v0.9.3 uses hub manifest caching for speed; use `--no-manifest-cache` to force fresh index fetch
simon: reproduced locally with the same command. stack trace shows it fails before weight key normalization. logs:
```
2026-03-19T14:22:11Z ERROR converter.core: shard list len 4 != manifest.len 5
2026-03-19T14:22:11Z ERROR converter.core: aborting conversion: inconsistent safetensors index
``` 
simon: hypothesis: maintainer reuploaded shards and renamed final shard name (weight_map_4 -> weights_4) and manifest wasn't updated atomically; converter accepts the first manifest but hub returns payloads based on git LFS pointers — timing race
maya: workarounds that worked for me: 1) reclone repo to a fresh dir (no cache) 2) pass `--no-manifest-cache` 3) if still broken, download all `.safetensors` and run `--local-shards /path` to avoid hub manifest resolution
eli: on the quant regression side I dug into the converted checkpoint — several attention weight names were rewritten incorrectly (e.g., `attn.wq` -> `attn.query.weight` vs expected `self_attn.q_proj.weight`) which can silently miswire layers after key-mapping. That would explain the ppl jump
maya: ugh. the converter has a weight-rename table but it only applies after `revpin` resolution; if revpin points at a commit where keys had different names we end up with a mismatched mapping
simon: filing an issue/patch now — #4021: make key-rename mapping robust to revision pinning and add validation that sum of shard sizes == manifest.total_bytes before writing the RW artifact
simon: quick patch idea: when manifest vs payload count differs, download payload list using the git blob API and cross-check LFS pointers; if mismatch, fail with a clear message and suggest `--no-manifest-cache` or `--force-index-refresh`
maya: I've attached minimal repro steps in the issue and a tiny script to validate key-name deltas: https://redwood-internal/runs/4821-quant-eval (contains diff of key names and per-layer L2 between orig & converted)
ops-bot: created incident INC-1123 for conversion pipeline flakiness; assigned to eng-ml oncall
eli: next actions I propose: (1) add manifest integrity check early in converter, (2) add weight-name mapping unit tests against a handful of community model commits that have rename histories, (3) add an opt-in `--strict-key-check` that compares model architect signature (shapes + expected key regex) and aborts before quantize
maya: agreed. I'm holding the Dedicated bring-up until we have a validated convert of this model — current quantized artifact is unsafe for customers
simon: I'll land the manifest-check patch and the `--no-manifest-cache` flag in converter v0.9.4 today, will also push an eval rerun job
maya: thanks — ping me when the CI run finishes, will rerun the eval set. :thumbsup:
